chains.title: GABPA binds the alt allele more strongly and activates TERT

links.claim: GABPA has its own QBiC-SELEX model at this variant with predicted effect 4.01, meaning the alt A allele binds GABPA more strongly than the ref G allele; E16 is a GABPA-specific own-model lookup, not only a group-level Ets signal. GABPA is also an own-model passing member of Ets group G003 in E06, and I choose GABPA as the Ets factor because it has a GABPA-specific own-model prediction and is expressed in the glioblastoma context.

The variant lies in the TERT promoter PLS EH38E3622530, a promoter-like cCRE annotated at the TERT upstream promoter, so an allele-specific Ets-site change would occur in a promoter regulatory element.
TERT is the nearest protein-coding gene, 0.0 kb from the TSS, and the variant is annotated as a TERT upstream_gene_variant, making TERT the direct candidate target gene.

GABPA is expressed at 15.52 TPM in the DepMap glioblastoma subtype expression context used for the QBiC-SELEX screen. GABPA ChIP-seq peaks containing this variant exist in HepG2 and SK-N-SH, but not in glioblastoma, so glioblastoma occupancy at this element is not demonstrated; E03 cCRE z-scores are maxima over ENCODE biosamples and are not glioblastoma-specific.

TERT and TERT promoter mutations are implicated in glioblastoma and melanoma in the cited literature, but E04 does not provide GABPA-specific functional evidence or bladder-cancer evidence. The disease mechanism is therefore a prediction, not an established GABPA-dependent phenotype.

predictions: Allele-specific GABPA ChIP-qPCR shows higher GABPA occupancy on the alt A allele than on the ref G allele at chr5:1295113 in a glioblastoma-relevant cell line.
A TERT promoter ref-vs-alt reporter assay shows higher alt-allele activity in glioblastoma cells.
GABPA knockdown or CRISPRi reduces the alt-allele-dependent increase in TERT reporter activity or allele-specific TERT expression.
falsified_if: Allele-specific GABPA occupancy at chr5:1295113 is not observed in glioblastoma-relevant cells.
The alt allele does not increase TERT promoter activity or endogenous TERT expression in a GABPA-dependent manner.
GABPA knockdown or Ets-site mutation does not reduce the alt-allele effect.

chains.title: No TF-mediated effect of this variant
predictions: No allele-specific TF binding or TERT expression effect is attributable to this variant.
Any disease association is explained by a linked causal variant, a passenger event, or no functional allelic difference.
falsified_if: Allele-specific TF occupancy and allele-specific TERT expression are reproducibly demonstrated at this variant.
A linked variant is excluded and the single-base change alone alters TERT promoter activity in a TF-dependent manner.

chains.title: ETV5 binds the alt allele more strongly and activates TERT

links.claim: ETV5 is the best model in QBiC-SELEX Ets group G003, with own-model z 166.19 and predicted effect 2.121, meaning the alt A allele binds ETV5 more strongly than the ref G allele. I choose ETV5 within the Ets group because it is the group's best model and is expressed at 22.15 TPM in the glioblastoma context; no ETV5 ChIP-seq evidence at this site is provided.
The variant lies in the TERT promoter PLS EH38E3622530, so an allele-specific ETV5-site change would occur in a promoter regulatory element.
TERT is 0.0 kb from the TSS and is the direct candidate target gene.
ETV5 is expressed at 22.15 TPM in the DepMap glioblastoma subtype expression context, but no ETV5 ChIP-seq or perturbation data in glioblastoma are cited, so this is expression context only.

TERT is implicated in glioblastoma and melanoma in the cited literature, but E04 does not provide ETV5-specific functional evidence or bladder-cancer evidence. The ETV5-dependent disease mechanism is therefore predicted, not shown.

predictions: Allele-specific ETV5 ChIP-qPCR shows higher ETV5 occupancy on the alt A allele than on the ref G allele.
ETV5 knockdown or CRISPRi reduces alt-allele-driven TERT reporter activity or allele-specific TERT expression.
GABPA knockdown does not reduce the alt-allele effect if ETV5 is the functional factor.
falsified_if: Allele-specific ETV5 occupancy is not higher on the alt allele at chr5:1295113.
ETV5 knockdown or CRISPRi does not reduce alt-allele-driven TERT expression or reporter activity.
The alt-allele effect is fully explained by GABPA or another factor.

chains.title: Loss of ref-allele TFAP2A binding on the alt allele derepresses TERT

links.claim: TFAP2A has its own passing QBiC-SELEX model in AP-2 group G030 with z -28.06 and negative effect, meaning the ref G allele binds TFAP2A/AP-2 models more strongly than the alt A allele. I choose TFAP2A within the AP-2 group because it has an own-model prediction and is expressed at 9.65 TPM, whereas TFAP2B is 0.0 TPM and TFAP2E is 0.49 TPM.
The variant lies in the TERT promoter PLS EH38E3622530, so loss of an AP-2 site on the alt allele would alter a promoter regulatory element.
TERT is 0.0 kb from the TSS and is the direct candidate target gene.

TFAP2A is expressed at 9.65 TPM in the DepMap glioblastoma subtype expression context, but no TFAP2A ChIP-seq peak contains this variant in glioblastoma and there are 0 TFAP2A peaks within 100 bp without containing it; glioblastoma occupancy is therefore not supported by the cited ChIP evidence.

A repressive AP-2 site at the TERT promoter is not shown by any cited evidence. E04 links TERT to glioblastoma and melanoma generically but does not establish TFAP2A-mediated repression or derepression of TERT. The phenotype is therefore a hypothesis that requires direct repression evidence.

predictions: Allele-specific TFAP2A ChIP-qPCR shows higher TFAP2A occupancy on the ref G allele than on the alt A allele.
The alt allele reduces TFAP2A binding in an allele-specific reporter or MPRA assay.
TFAP2A knockdown or CRISPRi increases TERT expression if this AP-2 site is repressive.
falsified_if: TFAP2A occupancy is not higher on the ref G allele than on the alt A allele at chr5:1295113.
The alt allele does not reduce TFAP2A binding in an allele-specific assay.
TFAP2A knockdown does not increase TERT expression in glioblastoma-relevant cells, or TFAP2A does not repress this TERT promoter element.

grades_v0.reason: E06 does list GABPA as a passing member of Ets group G003 with its own model (z 68.47) and group direction alt>ref; however this is an in vitro QBiC-SELEX prediction with no allele-specific ChIP, reporter or MPRA evidence. The group's best model is ETV5, so GABPA's direction is inferred from its own passing model within a group, not from a GABPA-specific allele comparison beyond SELEX.
E01 annotates ENSR5_832QG promoter and upstream_gene_variant for TERT; E03 places the variant inside PLS EH38E3622530. Both directly show a promoter element containing the variant.
E02 lists TERT at 0.0 kb from the TSS and E01 gives TERT as the transcript consequence, so TERT is the direct candidate target.

E06 gives GABPA 15.52 TPM in the DepMap glioblastoma subtype context, which is expression-only. The claim itself concedes no direct ChIP-seq in tumor cells. E03's cCRE z-scores are maxima across ENCODE biosamples and are explicitly not biosample-specific, so promoter activity in glioblastoma cells is not shown.

E04 is a broad Europe PMC search dominated by melanoma reviews and clinically oriented papers; only PMID 42804732 directly concerns a TERT promoter-mutant glioblastoma cohort and PMID 42859331 concerns TERT promoter wild-type GBM. There is no bladder cancer evidence and no functional evidence that GABPA-dependent TERT activation drives disease. The mechanistic half of the claim is a prediction, not cited evidence.

E06 shows ELF1 as a passing own-model member of the same Ets group G003 (z 124.32, alt>ref). This is a binding prediction only, and ELF1 is not distinguished from GABPA by any allele-specific or perturbation data.
E01 (promoter feature) and E03 (PLS EH38E3622530 containing the variant) directly support a promoter element.
E02 places TERT at the TSS (0.0 kb), making it the direct target.
ELF1 expression at 17.41 TPM in the glioblastoma DepMap context (E06) is expression context only; no occupancy in glioblastoma cells is cited and E03 is cross-biosample.
Same problem as H1: E04 is a generic TERT/disease literature set with no ELF1-specific or functional data, and no bladder cancer evidence.

E09 shows TFAP2A as a passing own-model member of AP-2 group G030 with z -28.06 and negative effect (alt binds less, i.e. ref>alt), which matches the claim's direction. However this is a QBiC-SELEX prediction with no allele-specific occupancy or reporter data.
E01 and E03 directly place the variant in a TERT promoter PLS.
E02 places TERT 0.0 kb from the TSS.
TFAP2A expression at 9.65 TPM in the DepMap glioblastoma context (E09) is expression-only. The additional premise that an AP-2 site here is repressive is not supported by any cited evidence.

The phenotype claim rests on 'derepression of TERT after loss of TFAP2A binding', but no cited source shows TFAP2A represses TERT or occupies this element. E04 bears only on generic TERT/disease association and does not say what the claim says about AP-2-mediated repression.

grades_final.reason: E16 provides a GABPA own-model QBiC-SELEX prediction (effect 4.01, alt binds more) and E06 confirms GABPA as a passing own-model member of Ets group G003, but this is only an in vitro binding prediction. No allele-specific GABPA occupancy, reporter, MPRA, or perturbation evidence is cited.
E01 annotates the variant as an upstream TERT promoter-region variant and E03 places it in promoter-like cCRE EH38E3622530, directly supporting the element claim.
E02 places TERT at 0.0 kb from its TSS, and E01 annotates the variant as a TERT upstream_gene_variant, directly supporting TERT as the nearest candidate target gene.

E06 supports GABPA expression in the DepMap glioblastoma subtype context (15.52 TPM), and E17 supports absence of glioblastoma GABPA ChIP-seq peaks containing the variant. However, E17 also notes peaks in HepG2/SK-N-SH and warns absence may reflect missing experiments, while E03 z-scores are maxima over biosamples, not glioblastoma-specific. This is expression and absence-of-occupancy context, not glioblastoma functional evidence.

E04 provides generic TERT/telomerase and TERT promoter literature in glioblastoma and melanoma, but no GABPA-specific functional evidence and no bladder-cancer evidence. The claim itself correctly states this is a prediction, so it is indirect rather than established.

E06 identifies ETV5 as the best own-model member of Ets group G003 with z 166.19 and effect 2.121, indicating the alt allele binds ETV5 more strongly in QBiC-SELEX. This is a strong in vitro binding prediction but remains only a binding prediction; no ETV5 ChIP, reporter, MPRA, or perturbation evidence is cited.
E01 and E03 directly place the variant in the TERT promoter PLS EH38E3622530.
E02 places TERT 0.0 kb from its TSS and E01 annotates the variant as a TERT upstream_gene_variant.

E06 supports ETV5 expression at 22.15 TPM in the DepMap glioblastoma subtype context, but no ETV5 ChIP-seq or perturbation data in glioblastoma are cited. This is expression context only, not functional occupancy or perturbation in the disease cell type.

E04 generically links TERT/telomerase to glioblastoma and melanoma, but provides no ETV5-specific functional evidence and no bladder-cancer evidence. The ETV5-dependent disease mechanism is therefore indirect and predicted, not shown.

E09 shows TFAP2A as an own-model passing member of AP-2 group G030 with z -28.06 and negative effect, consistent with the ref allele binding TFAP2A/AP-2 more strongly than the alt allele. However, the best model is TFAP2E, and the evidence is a QBiC-SELEX binding prediction only; no allele-specific TFAP2A occupancy or functional assay is cited.
E01 and E03 directly place the variant in the TERT promoter PLS EH38E3622530.
E02 places TERT 0.0 kb from its TSS and E01 annotates the variant as a TERT upstream_gene_variant.

E09 supports TFAP2A expression at 9.65 TPM in the DepMap glioblastoma subtype context, but E18 reports no glioblastoma TFAP2A ChIP-seq peak containing the variant and no peaks within 100 bp. E18 also cautions that absence may reflect missing experiments. Glioblastoma TFAP2A occupancy at this element is therefore not demonstrated, and the cell-type link is context-only.

E04 provides only generic TERT/glioblastoma/melanoma literature and no evidence that TFAP2A binds this element repressively or that loss of ref-allele TFAP2A binding derepresses TERT. The TFAP2A-mediated derepression phenotype is not supported by the cited evidence.

checks.why: Returns GABPA's own-model SELEX z and predicted effect at this variant, confirming whether GABPA-specific (not just group-level) direction is alt>ref and whether it is own_model.
Tests whether GABPA actually occupies this promoter element in a glioblastoma biosample, which E03 cannot show because its z-scores are cross-biosample maxima.
Tests whether TFAP2A occupies the TERT promoter at all in relevant cells, directly probing the unsupported repressor premise of H3.

In the group rows, 'own model' means the TF has its own QBiC-SELEX model and 'mapped' that it is covered only through CIS-BP-mapped models of related TFs. A TF not named in any group row may still have its own model, even one that passes the gate: look it up with qbic_tf_detail before stating its coverage or a QBiC-SELEX direction for it. predicted_effect > 0 means the alternate allele binds more strongly.
